newsitem.title: USA: LATIN AMERICAN SOCCER PLAYERS CHARGED WITH RAPE.
newsitem.headline: LATIN AMERICAN SOCCER PLAYERS CHARGED WITH RAPE.

text.p: Two Latin American players from Washington's D.C. United soccer team have been charged in the alleged rape of a Columbus woman following a weekend match, officials said on Tuesday.
Raul Diaz Arce, 27, of San Miguel, El Salvador, and Michael Jose Gori, 24, of Rosario, Argentina, were freed on Monday after posting $25,000 cash bond each in Franklin County Municipal Court.
Judge Scott VanDerKarr ordered them to return to court on Aug. 29 for a preliminary hearing. Failure to show for the hearing would result in each forfeiting $500,000 bonds.
The incident allegedly occurred while the two were in Columbus last weekend for a match.

Arce, who is tied for the league scoring lead, and Gori, a defensive mainstay, were charged with assaulting the woman in a room at the Crowne Plaza Hotel where they were staying after playing the Columbus Crew on Saturday night.
The woman alleged that Arce held her down while Gori raped her. Police charged Gori with rape and Arce with complicity to rape.
She said she had met them in a bar early on Sunday and they offered to let her use the telephone in their hotel room. She was treated at Riverside Methodist Hospital after the incident.
